# Spacewave

> Spacewave is a local-first app for Spaces: Drives, Git repositories, canvases
> and other objects that sync between a person's devices. Agents use Spacewave
> through the `spacewave` command-line interface (CLI). This file tells you how
> to install the CLI, connect it to the person's account, and work in the Space
> they are looking at.

A person usually sends you here with a prompt copied from the Spacewave app.
It carries either a pairing code or a desktop socket path, and the Space ID,
object key and path they had open. Follow the steps in order. Ask the person
only when a step below says to.

## 1. Fit the project you are in

Before you write anything, look at the working directory: its version control
ignore rules, tool directories such as `.tmp/`, `bin/` or `.tools/`, and agent
instruction files such as `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`. Put files where this
project already keeps downloaded tools, and follow its conventions for notes.

## 2. Get the CLI

If `spacewave` is on PATH, use it. Otherwise stage a copy in an ignored tool
directory of this project, for example `.tmp/bin/spacewave`. Confirm the
directory is ignored first (`git check-ignore -v .tmp/bin/spacewave`). Outside
a Git repository, use `~/.local/bin`.

Release assets live at
`https://github.com/s4wave/spacewave/releases/latest/download/<asset>`:

| System | Asset |
|---|---|
| macOS, Apple silicon | `spacewave-cli-macos-arm64.zip` |
| macOS, Intel | `spacewave-cli-macos-amd64.zip` |
| Linux, x86-64 | `spacewave-cli-linux-amd64.tar.gz` |
| Linux, ARM64 | `spacewave-cli-linux-arm64.tar.gz` |
| Windows, x86-64 | `spacewave-cli-windows-amd64.zip` |

Download the asset and `checksums.txt` from the same URL, check the SHA-256 of
the asset against its line in `checksums.txt`, and extract the `spacewave`
binary (`spacewave.exe` on Windows) into the tool directory. Run
`spacewave --help` to confirm it works.

## 3. Connect to the account

Leave the CLI's state in its default location. Every agent on this computer
then shares one background service and one connected account, and later agents
skip pairing.

Flags belong to the command level that defines them, so set shared options
through the environment instead. `SPACEWAVE_OUTPUT=json` makes every command
print JSON; parse it instead of text.

First check whether the account is already here:

```sh
export SPACEWAVE_OUTPUT=json
spacewave session list
```

If a session already reaches the Space named in the prompt, use its index and
go to step 4.

### With a desktop socket path

The Spacewave desktop app is running and already holds the account. Set
`SPACEWAVE_SOCKET_PATH` to the path from the prompt for every command. No
pairing or approval is needed.

### With a pairing code

```sh
spacewave login p2p --code <CODE> --label "<your name> on <host name>"
```

Use a label the person will recognize, such as "Claude Code on build-box". The
command connects to the person's Spacewave window, prints six emoji, and waits.
Show the person the six emoji and ask them to check that the same six appear in
Spacewave, then approve there. The command ends when they approve and prints
the new session's index. With `SPACEWAVE_OUTPUT=json` it prints the emoji and
the session as JSON lines.

The command blocks until the person approves, so you must show the emoji while
it runs. Run it in the background with its output in a file, for example
`.tmp/spacewave-pair.log`, read the emoji from that file, tell the person, and
then wait for the command to exit.

If the command reports that the code expired or pairing was rejected, ask the
person for a new prompt from the Connect an agent button. Codes last ten
minutes and work once.

The paired session has the same access as the person's account. The person can
remove it at any time from Sessions in the app.

## 4. Work in the Space

Select the session and Space once through the environment:

```sh
export SPACEWAVE_SESSION_INDEX=<N> SPACEWAVE_SPACE=<space-id>
spacewave space list
spacewave space info <space-id>
spacewave space object list
spacewave fs ls <object-key>
spacewave fs cat <object-key>/-/<path>
spacewave fs write --from ./file <object-key>/-/<path>
```

Object paths put `/-/` between the object key and a path inside it. The
command groups `git`, `canvas`, `vm` and others work on their object kinds; run
`spacewave <group> --help` for their commands.

A local-only account syncs from the person's other devices. If a read waits,
the person's Spacewave window may be closed; ask them to open it.

## 5. Leave a note for the next agent

Record how you connected (the CLI location, the session index and the Space ID)
where this project keeps agent notes, so the next agent reuses them.
